script.base: No spread, total, or kickoff weather is saved, so this is a form read only. LA's offense is the more intact unit: Adams has 29 targets, 358 yards and 498 air yards, and the backfield is a Kyren/Corum split (38/214 and 28/148). PHI's defense allows about 6.75 YPA (left 7.21 on 24, middle 7.25 on 24, right 6.18 on 40) and 4.09 rush YPC, with S Epps and LB Baun out. PHI's own pass game is gutted (Smith 27/235, Brown, and Goedert all out), so the base flow is LA moving the ball through Adams and the run split while PHI leans on Barkley (34/174) and Hurts (14/89) and dumps leftover targets to Wicks (15/179). Competitive to LA-leaning, not an assumed blowout.
script.flip1: PHI's 26% blitz climbs and Stafford's -0.23 EPA/db vs blitz (vs +0.22 with no blitz) shows up. Deep Adams yards fall back toward the Week-1 26, and checkdowns lift Higbee and Kyren catches. That pressure flip is the main way the Adams over dies while the Higbee over can still live.
script.flip2: LA gets ahead and kills the clock with Kyren (recent rush lines 85 and 88) and Corum, so both LA receiving overs stall. The reverse flip is PHI grinding Barkley (83 and 82 yard games) behind a Donald-less LA front, LA chasing, Adams volume up and a run-clock read dead.

PHI T Fred Johnson Out (knee) is an OL hit: pressure up, rush efficiency down, more quick throws. PHI S Marcus Epps Out (groin) and LB Zack Baun Out (concussion) are the LA-offense gifts: Epps helps deep shots (Adams, 498 air yards), Baun helps TE/RB/slot (Higbee, Kyren receiving). LA TE Terrance Ferguson Out (ankle, 12 tgt/63 yds) funnels to Higbee (13/74); TE Colby Parkinson is Questionable (knee) and can steal that share. LA DT Aaron Donald Out (back) softens the run front for Barkley but is offset by Johnson being out. LA CB Jaylen Watson Out (shoulder) is a crack for PHI WRs; LA LB Josaiah Stewart Questionable (groin) is a pass-rush maybe. No inactives lock in the pack.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and both overs lost. PHI lived in the blitz, Stafford's -0.23 EPA versus pressure showed up, and Adams repeated the Week-1 26 while the replacement for Epps and a bracket took the deep middle away. Higbee's real role was the 12-yard game: Parkinson took Ferguson's 12 targets, and once LA had a lead it ran Kyren (85, 88) and Corum instead of throwing into the middle. The coin-flip prices were the market already holding the blitz plan and the committee, and 195/137 plus the 62 were explosives a 4.09-YPC clock game did not need. That counter is real enough to flag Adams and keep Higbee at a lean, not strong enough to drop the primary-target overlap.
slip_story: One story: LA pass volume against PHI's middle/left leak with Epps and Baun out. Adams (deep primary) and Higbee (Ferguson-vacated TE) are the two legs, one market each, no TDs, no depth receivers. They share pass volume and split only if the blitz flip hits. Do not add a total under, a Kyren rush over, or a Barkley rush over to this slip. Wicks over is the PHI-chase leg and belongs on a different ticket if the human wants it.
